Preserve and restore a real backup using Plex-supported recovery, verify service restart/version changes and database integrity, and handle authenticated identity without exporting tokens or allowing the service to mutate or erase unrelated library content.

v31Hardening.title: AMP signed provenance, updates, controller, and private instance lifecycle
v31Hardening.trigger: Before changing the pinned package version or hash, accepting an upstream signed package path, managing AMP services/timers or firewall exposure, creating ADS/controller instances, handling credentials/license inputs, or migrating real instance and game data. Prove publisher provenance and supported backup/restore while preserving operator-owned state.

v31Hardening.title: Selenium browser and driver deployment contract
v31Hardening.trigger: Only if the owner asks RIDE to manage a Selenium browser, driver, Grid, or browser session path. Choose and pin the Server target, keep browser and driver artifacts within an owned deployment boundary, avoid downloading mutable binaries implicitly through Selenium Manager, and prove exact remove and preservation of consumer test data. The v3.0 binding RPM remains opt-in and does not claim a browser automation stack.

v31Hardening.title: SmartMonTools monitoring and device-selection lifecycle
v31Hardening.trigger: Before adding smartd activation, device selection, or status polling, define administrator-owned smartd.conf and service-state boundaries, ensure devices are selected explicitly, and prove no unowned storage state changes on disposable hardware or image fixtures. v3.0 manages the Fedora RPM only and leaves smartd stopped and disabled.

v31Hardening.title: ClamAV recurring updates, scan scope, and signature database retention
v31Hardening.trigger: Before adding scheduled updates, scanning, quarantine, or user-file access, define the service identity and update schedule, preserve unowned signature databases, bound scan roots and outputs, and prove failure/recovery on synthetic files without running against user data. v3.0 scope is one Fedora package install and one initial freshclam update only.

v31Hardening.title: NetworkMiner capture scope and extracted evidence handling
v31Hardening.trigger: Before enabling PCAP analysis or live capture, require authorized input/source scope, a disposable hostile-input fixture, private output location and size limits, credential and certificate handling, and cleanup/recovery evidence. v3.0 package setup only installs the verified application and does not open captures or listen for network traffic.

v31Hardening.title: Whole-system update target, reboot, and failure-path hardening
v31Hardening.trigger: Before widening Fedora target coverage or changing update policy, add exact-target evidence for repository outages, interrupted DNF transactions, reboot-required reporting and recovery guidance. Preserve the explicit preview, no-auto-reboot, and non-restorable contract; never retry a failed transaction before investigating its journal and DNF state.

v31Hardening.title: SSH reboot policy across sshd Match and account contexts
v31Hardening.trigger: Before expanding SSH reboot policy beyond the current named-principal Fedora 44 Workstation opt-in flow, test representative sshd Match and Include layouts, multiple named accounts, principal removal, and recovery when sshd policy or authorized_keys changes. The v3.0 operation remains opt-in and grants only /usr/bin/systemctl reboot to one explicitly supplied local user.

v31Hardening.title: BulkExtractor scan behavior, Snap interfaces, and evidence recovery
v31Hardening.trigger: Before RIDE processes forensic evidence with BulkExtractor or supports another target; verify the pinned Snap's declared and connected interfaces, use authorized synthetic disk-image fixtures including malformed inputs, bound outputs and resource use, and prove recovery without changing the source image. v3.0 installs the strict-confinement package only and does not open evidence.

v31Hardening.title: Email header analyzer parser, browser, and npm license review
v31Hardening.trigger: Before promoting package.email-header-analyzer beyond its v3.0 opt-in candidate: test synthetic normal, malformed, and large headers in a real browser; verify the route/hop analysis and confirm storage/network behavior stays local. Review resolved npm package licenses and install-script metadata against the pinned lockfile.

v31Hardening.title: Firefox global add-on updates, license metadata, and profile migration
v31Hardening.trigger: Before promoting setting.firefox-addons beyond an opt-in candidate or widening beyond Fedora 44 Workstation: review current AMO license metadata for the full 16-item list, test how Firefox updates and removes globally installed add-ons in seeded profiles, and verify replacement/update recovery without changing unrelated profile data.

v31Hardening.title: Browser forensic artifact parity and real-profile review
v31Hardening.trigger: Before promoting package.browser-forensic beyond an opt-in candidate or changing its source pin: add synthetic fixtures for downloads, form history, extensions, preferences, and sessions where the upstream CLI supports them; verify parser coverage and unchanged input hashes; review profile-copy and secret-output recovery using disposable user data. Keep real profile data out of automated transcripts.

v31Hardening.title: Keyfile mount record variants and concurrent configuration recovery
v31Hardening.trigger: Before supporting mapper names, keyfile paths or fstab/crypttab record forms outside the v3.0 contract, test escaped fields, optional key source suffixes, multiple related records, and concurrent system configuration writers on a disposable encrypted data volume. Preserve active/mounted refusal and exact recovery.

v31Hardening.title: VMFS6 reader lifecycle and fixture-backed validation
v31Hardening.trigger: The owner deferred the genuine VMFS6 fixture test from v3.0 to v3.1. Before claiming VMFS6 access, obtain an authorized image with a known file manifest, pin and review the reader source, prove Fedora 44 opens the image read-only and leaves its digest unchanged, and exercise plan, opt-in gate, apply, repeat, status, restore, and explicit removal in a disposable VM. Keep the experimental archived reader isolated, reject block devices and symlinks, and review VMFS5 separately. The v3.0 opt-in install candidate does not establish VMFS6 access.
